title: Sustainability and health
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:38Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 may adapt geo-sustainability-means, but is not highly sure, so to the Opus match check
2026-11-01T14:56:01Z confirm: Claude Opus 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

changes: Replace the fishing and bushland examples with examples that link sustainability to health and human development, as the VCE Health and Human Development course uses them.
Add a sentence tying the three areas of sustainability (environment, economy and society) to health and human development for future generations.
match.reason: The bank card teaches the same three-area idea of sustainability that the new point needs, but its examples and framing are geographic rather than about health, so it needs health-focused examples.

confirm.reason: The Geography card defines sustainability and its three areas but never links them to health and human development, which is the core of this VCE point, so linking them would add a new step rather than a small change.

draft.title: Sustainability and health
card: Sustainability means meeting the needs of people today without harming the ability of future generations to meet theirs. It helps health and human development last over time.
protecting natural resources, such as clean air, water and soil, so that they last. People need these to stay healthy.
keeping communities fair and connected, with access to education, health care and safe housing for all people, now and later.
using money and resources in ways that can continue, so that jobs, income and services can keep supporting health over time.
draft.remember: Sustainability protects the environment, community and economy so that health can last for future generations.

a.q: A town protects its river from pollution so that its water stays safe for children in the future. Which type of sustainability is this?
a.why: The town is protecting a natural resource, its river water, so it lasts. Social sustainability is about fair and connected communities, which is not the focus here.
a.clue: What is being protected: nature, people's access or money?

b.q: A government builds a clinic in a poor rural area and trains local staff, and funds it each year from a steady budget. Which type of sustainability does the yearly funding best show?
b.why: Funding from a steady budget lets the service keep going over time, which is economic sustainability. Building the clinic for poor communities supports social sustainability, which is tempting, but the question asks about the funding.
b.clue: Focus on the yearly funding, not on who uses the clinic.
